text:
maria: Quick follow-up on the dequant fusion conversation. Need to land shape/ABI rules so the runtime can choose fused kernels safely.
kevin: Yep. Biggest headache is when a fused op leaves KV cache in a packed/int4 layout and later consumers expect unpacked fp16. We need an explicit per-tensor header.
sam: Sketch for QuantHeader we can attach to tensors (small immutable struct):
```
QuantHeader: dtype (int8|int4|fp8e4m3|fp16),
            scale: float,
            zero_point: int,
            pack_layout: ("contig"|"blocked"|"nqk_packed"),
            opset: "qv1"|"qv2"
```
If kernels accept QuantHeader, fusion can be used; otherwise runtime inserts dequant steps.
maria: Questions: who owns opset evolution? And can kernels mutate header bytes?
kevin: Runtime/eng-runtime owns opset semantics. Kernels should not mutate headers in-place if entries are shared by cache readers. Instead kernels can emit a small "HeaderDelta" describing logical changes (e.g., unified_scale), and runtime applies it lazily.
nayana: Perf note: allocating headers per tensor is cheap, but copying headers for every cache write loses zero-copy. The HeaderDelta/lazy-apply idea lets kernels write raw bytes and return a delta pointer. Runtime materializes deltas only on mismatch.
sam: We also need per-argument consumption rules for kernels. Proposal: three-state per-arg policy: MUST_QUANT, ACCEPTS_QUANT, MUST_BE_DEQUANT. Example:
```
sig = { q: MUST_QUANT, k: MUST_QUANT, v: ACCEPTS_QUANT }
```
Runtime synthesizes plan: if an arg is ACCEPTS_QUANT but upstream is dequantized, runtime may skip conversion.
maria: Registry API sketch: register_kernel(name, arg_policies, produces_header: bool, accepts_header: bool, supports_inplace_unpack: bool, est_latency_ms, est_convert_cost_ms).
kevin: And we should let kernels optionally write into KV cache in-place. Contract for cache entries becomes: (raw_bytes, shape, QuantHeader, writer_opset). Readers always check header+opset and pick a kernel or trigger lazy unpack/dequant.
infra-bot: CI checklist item added: "cache compatibility matrix tests" (int4<->fp16, fp8<->int8, blocked->contig).
nayana: On INT4 packing: random-access indexing often requires unpack before GEMM. Options: (A) Hot fused kernels implement fast in-register unpack (best latency), (B) runtime unpacks to fp16 before calling generic kernels (simpler fallback). Registry should flag supports_inplace_unpack so planner can favor option A for low-latency paths.
sam: Edge case: mixed-precision inputs from upstream (Q in fp8, K in int8). We should support partial fusion: e.g., fused_qk_quant_dequant that handles q/k combination and emits a common format for attention, with v handled separately. Kernels need to declare which subsets they operate on quantized.
maria: Compatibility scoring: runtime builds candidate kernels and computes score = est_latency_ms + conversion_penalty_ms + cache_mismatch_penalty. Pick min score; if score > baseline_fp16_kernel * 1.2 then prefer conservative path and emit telemetry.
kevin: Telemetry we must record: chosen_kernel, opset_used, total_convert_ms, bytes_moved, cache_mismatch (bool). That helps prioritize kernel work.
sam: Testing plan: automated microbench across shapes seq=[16,128,1024], batch=[1,16,64], d_model=[512,2048], measure perf and numeric delta against fp16 baseline within tolerance. Add packed-block layout correctness tests including attention masks and padding behavior.
nayana: Also add unit tests that intentionally mix opsets and assert runtime chooses safe fallback or performs lazy delta application.
maria: Rollout plan: gate any new fused kernel behind an opset flag + canary on Dedicated. If telemetry shows regressions, opset flag lets us revert without model changes.
kevin: I'll draft the QuantHeader/Delta RFC and start a kernel-registry change PR that includes per-arg policy enums and supports_inplace_unpack.
infra-bot: Created canary group "int4-fp8-experiments" on Dedicated clusters.
maria: Action items recap: kevin -> QuantHeader + opset bump rules (EOD Fri), sam -> registry API PR + planning logic (WIP), nayana -> CI tests for packing/compatibility, infra-bot -> canary group done. Keep follow-ups here. :thumbsup:
